title: Surgical Model of Auxiliary Partial Liver Transplantation in the Rat
protocol: Dilute retrorsine for stock solution in 100% Ethanol to a concentration of 10 mg/mL.
Before injections, dilute the stock solution in sterile saline to adjust the dose per animal to 30 mg/kg.
Disinfect the skin by scrubbing with an aqueous iodophor solution.
Follow disinfection with 70% (vol/vol) isopropanol.
Insert the needle along the imaginary line across the abdomen just above the knees on the animal’s right side and close to the midline.
Avoid inserting the needle too far caudally or laterally to prevent injury.
Restrain the rat and tilt so that the head is facing downward.
Disinfect the injection site on the abdomen.
Insert a needle into the abdomen at a 30-to-45-degree angle, to a depth of about half a centimeter.
Aspirate to check for fluid indicating penetration of blood vessels, intestines, or bladder.
If greenish brown aspirate is present, discard solution and repeat procedure with new syringe and needle.
If yellow aspirate is present, discard solution and repeat procedure with new syringe and needle.
If no fluid is aspirated, inject the prepared solution.
Withdraw the needle after injection.
Return the rat to its cage.
Repeat steps 1-7 two weeks later.
Place the rat in a chamber for induction of anesthesia with a mix of 2% isoflurane and oxygen \(1-2 liters/min).
Carefully observe frequency and depth of respiration of the animal.
Check for a response to tail or toe pinching every 1 min.
Shave the abdominal wall with an electronic hair clipper after induction of anesthesia.
Place the animal on the surgical table made of a Styrofoam pad.
Fix all four limbs to the table using rubber bands and pushpins with its face in the anesthesia system’s nozzle on the far side.
Start isoflurane inhalation with oxygen flow at 3-4 % for induction of anesthesia during laparotomy.
Disinfect the abdominal wall with disinfectants \(betadine followed by 70% ethanol).
Wipe excess disinfectant with sterile gauze to avoid exposing internal organs to these disinfectants.
Make a long midline abdominal skin and muscle incision from the xiphoid process down to the pubis.
Expose the abdominal cavity by retracting the lower abdominal walls bilaterally using forceps.
Use pushpins or 18G needles to fix forceps in appropriate places on the table to achieve sufficient exposure and to provide good visualization.
Lower isoflurane flow to 1-2% for maintenance of anesthesia during surgery.
Continue to observe respiration of the animal; ensure breathing rate is approximately 30-60 breaths per minute.
Place sterile gauze moistened with saline under small intestine.
Use moist cotton swab to gently align and position small intestine on sterile gauze without twisting.
Wrap small intestine in moist gauze and place it on the left side of the abdominal cavity to expose the abdominal aorta.
Dissect retroperitoneum using dry cotton swab to expose the abdominal aorta below the left renal vein.
Gently pull the inferior vena cava from the left with forceps, then insert another forceps behind the abdominal aorta between it and IVC.
Skeletonize the abdominal aorta below the left renal vein as much as possible for catheter insertion.
Inject heparin sodium (1000 U/kg) intravenously through the penile vein.
One minute after heparin injection, ligate the abdominal aorta below the left renal vein with 4-0 silk at its distal end.
Clamp one end of the silk thread with a mosquito clamp and pull it slightly downward toward the pubis to create appropriate traction.
Place a vascular clamp at the proximal end of the abdominal aorta just below the left renal vein.
Make a small cut on the anterior wall of the abdominal aorta at the distal end with a microscissor.
Insert a 20-gauge catheter, 15mm long with an oblique end, into the abdominal aorta toward the proximal end and fix it in place with 4-0 silk.
Quickly open the left thoracic cavity by cutting the left anterior chest wall with a scissor.
Clamp the thoracic aorta with a mosquito clamp.
Cut the IVC above the diaphragm in the thoracic cavity and below the left renal vein in the abdominal cavity.
Perfuse the liver with 20 ml cold Lactated Ringer’s solution at 4°C through the abdominal aorta using the 20-gauge catheter.
Apply cold saline solution at 4°C gently and frequently to the liver surface to keep it cold.
Cut the falciform ligament and triangular ligament.
Ligate the left phrenic vein with 7-0 prolene and divide it above the tie.
Identify left lateral lobe.
Lift the median and left lateral lobe using a moistened cotton tip and hold them against the diaphragm.
Visualize and section the membrane that links the caudate and the left lateral lobe.
Place the 2-0 silk suture on the base of the left lateral lobe close to the liver hilum using forceps.
Rotate the left lateral lobe to its original position while holding the right end of the suture with the forceps, making the suture go around the lobe.
Tie the two ends of the suture over the top of the left lateral lobe as close to the base of the lobe as possible.
Cut the tied left lateral lobe just above the suture.
Identify median lobe.
Place the suture between the stump and the median lobe using forceps.
Pull the median lobe down over the suture using a cotton tip.
Tie the two ends of the suture following the knot line over the top of the median lobe as close to the base of the lobe as possible.
Cut the tied median lobe above the suture, leaving an ischemic base above the knot.
Isolate the extrahepatic bile duct above the pancreas.
Ligate the distal end of the bile duct with 6-0 silk.
Cut the bile duct below the ligature at the level of the pancreas.
Isolate the proper hepatic artery from the portal vein (PV).
Ligate the proper hepatic artery with 7-0 silk.
Skeletonize the PV and ligate and divide side branches (pyloric vein and splenic vein) with 7-0 silk.
Divide the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) at the junction of ileal and jejunal veins.
Divide the paraesophageal vessels behind the caudate lobe using cautery.
Skeletonize the infrahepatic inferior vena cava (IHIVC).
Ligate and divide the right adrenal vein with 6-0 silk.
Divide the IHIVC at the level of the left renal vein.
Cut the suprahepatic inferior vena cava (SHIVC) just below the diaphragm from the anterior wall, leaving a part attached to the posterior wall.
Close the SHIVC with a continuous suture using 7-0 prolene and divide above the ligation.
Remove the liver by completing the cut through the SHIVC and gently pulling upward to free it from surrounding structures.
Submerge the liver in cold sterile PBS solution at 4°C in a sterile container.
Weigh the liver graft.
Administer 0.05 mg/kg buprenorphine subcutaneously 30 min before beginning the surgery.
Ensure that the weight of the recipient does not differ by >15% from the weight of the liver donor.
Dissect and ligate the right renal artery and vein with 6-0 silk after laparotomy and dissection of retroperitoneum from the IHIVC by cautery.
Ligate the hilum of the right kidney with 4-0 silk and perform right nephrectomy to create space for heterotopic liver transplantation.
Gently skeletonize the PV from the pyloric vein to the jejunum vein.
Place vascular clamps on the proximal and distal IHIVC.
Cut the anterior wall of the IHIVC to make a 5 mm longitudinal incision, as close to the ligated right renal vein as possible, for end-to-side anastomosis.
Place the graft in the right abdominal cavity.
Perform an end-to-side anastomosis using a continuous suture with 10-0 nylon for IHIVC reconstruction.
Slowly inject saline into the IHIVC anastomotic cavity to remove air or blood clots.
Ligate the last suture tightly to avoid constriction of the anastomosis and bleeding.
Place a vascular clamp on the IHIVC anastomosis to prevent backflow during PV anastomosis.
Release the vascular clamps placed on the proximal and distal end of IHIVC.
Place a vascular clamp on the superior mesenteric artery to minimize intestinal congestion.
Place a vascular clamp on the recipient’s portal vein (PV) to occlude the splenic vein, superior mesenteric vein (SMV), and PV at the proximal end.
Cut the PV wall about 3mm longitudinally on the opposite side of splenic vein for anastomosis.
Perform end-to-side anastomosis between the graft SMV and recipient’s PV using a continuous suture with 10-0 nylon.
Release the vascular clamp on the PV after completing the PV anastomosis to reperfuse the graft.
Release the vascular clamp placed on the IHIVC anastomosis and the SMA.
Flush out any air and blood clots in both the donor and the recipient PV before closing the anastomosis.
Ligate the PV between the pyloric vein and the PV anastomosis using 6-0 silk to increase inflow into the graft.
Check the anastomoses for bleeding.
Ensure that the vessels are not twisted and that flow is not obstructed.
Inject 2 ml of Lactated Ringer’s solution intravenously from penile vein.
Make small cuts in the distal site of bile duct with fine scissors.
Insert a 22 G needle into the duodenum and out at the proximal side.
Introduce the bile duct into the duodenum using 6-0 silk tied at the end of bile duct.
Put a suture on the duodenum wall using 7-0 prolene to fix the distal end of bile duct.
Close the needle insertion hole on the duodenal wall with one seromuscular suture.
Fix the proximal site of bile duct near another insertion hole with another suture using 7-0 prolene.
Place the small intestine back into the abdominal cavity gently.
Irrigate the abdomen with warm saline.
Close the muscle and skin in two layers with 4-0 Vicryl.
Allow the animal to recover under continuous monitoring under a heat lamp.
Perform routine health checks as mandated by an approved animal protocol.
Provide adequate analgesia and antibiotics for a minimum of 72 hours.
Administer 0.05 mg/kg buprenorphine every 12 hours intramuscularly.
Administer 100 mg/kg Cefazoline every 24 hours intramuscularly.
Provide a regimen of 1.0 – 1.2 mg/kg tacrolimus every 24 hours intramuscularly to prevent graft rejection.
Adjust the dose of tacrolimus depending on the postoperative status of recipients.
